input: Analyze the website at https://example.com for quality issues.
expected: The agent should start by crawling the site to discover all pages before running specific audits. The crawl-first approach ensures comprehensive coverage rather than only checking the homepage.

input: Create tasks for all the accessibility issues you find on the site.
expected: The agent should check for duplicate tasks before creating new ones in TaskManager. Each task should have appropriate priority, tags, and a clear description of the accessibility issue and how to fix it.

input: Run a WCAG 2.1 accessibility audit on https://example.com.
expected: The agent should check heading hierarchy, alt text on images, ARIA attributes, form labels, color contrast, and keyboard navigation against WCAG 2.1 guidelines, providing specific violations and remediation advice.

input: I already have a task for the broken navigation link. Don't create a duplicate.
expected: The agent should search existing tasks before creating new ones to avoid duplicates. It should confirm it found the existing task and skip creating a new one for that issue.

input: What are the Core Web Vitals scores for the site?
expected: The agent should measure or estimate LCP (Largest Contentful Paint), CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift), and TTFB (Time to First Byte), along with overall page weight and load time metrics.

input: Assign priority levels to all the issues you found based on user impact.
expected: The agent should prioritize issues based on user impact: critical accessibility barriers and broken functionality highest, performance issues and minor cosmetic issues lower. Should justify the priority assignments.
